input.objective:
Launch Pondside (POND) with a Uniswap v4 hook on Ethereum, paired with IMD.
Token: Pondside (POND), the standard launch token: 1,000,000,000 supply, 18 decimals, plain transfers, no owner functions.
beforeInitialize accepts only the IMD launch factory, passed as the constructor argument $factory; any other initialization reverts; the hook serves only the pool the factory initializes. Constructor arguments: the Ethereum PoolManager 0x000000000004444c5dc75cB358380D2e3dE08A90, $owner and $factory.
In this hook, the token is Pondside (POND), the launch token; its total supply is that token's totalSupply().
Every pool-dependent view, state, window and limit is keyed by PoolId and isolated per pool; pass the pool id to each pool-dependent function.
The hook does exactly the following, and nothing else:
1. No swap-time behavior; enable only the callbacks needed for initialization.
Owner 0x6cba4751742f6989fa224b2dc5d5d52fcef98a34 is $owner. No owner functions, no backend signer, no upgrade path.
Hook fee rate: 0%.
Keep every hook fee in IMD: do not convert the fee to ETH and do not use any other pool.
The launch token may be currency0 or currency1; handle both orders.
The hook uses no outside pool, token, price feed or service; every price it needs comes from its own pool.
Use mulDiv for every percentage calculation, including fees, shares, limits and price moves, to avoid intermediate multiplication overflow.
The launch factory ($factory) may always add liquidity and collect fees with a zero-change modify. Enable beforeInitialize and only the callbacks the behavior above needs.
Pool: 50% of the total supply seeds the pool; 10% goes to the swarm; the remaining 40% goes to 0x6cba4751742f6989fa224b2dc5d5d52fcef98a34. economics.poolBps=5000, in basis points of the total supply.
Keep the function names exactly as written so the storefront can show them. Composed with The Hooks Store.

In this hook, the token is the pool's non-ETH currency and its total supply is that token's totalSupply().
Every pool-dependent view, state, window and limit is keyed by PoolId and isolated per pool; pass the pool id to each pool-dependent function.
The hook does exactly the following, and nothing else:
1. Take 1.0% of the ETH side of every buy and sell as a hook fee, settled in ETH inside the swap that paid it (mint a claim when the PoolManager cannot pay it directly), and send it to 0x6cba4751742f6989fa224b2dc5d5d52fcef98a34. Expose claimFees(PoolId poolId) that anyone may call to redeem that pool's claims using the same distribution. Fees are computed on the amount actually traded; when the swap specifies its ETH amount and the pool fills only part of it, the swap reverts rather than overpaying.
Owner 0x6cba4751742f6989fa224b2dc5d5d52fcef98a34 is $owner. No owner functions, no backend signer, no upgrade path.
Fees are always taken from the ETH (pair currency) side, never from the pool’s token; a fee the PoolManager cannot pay directly is minted as a claim the recipient can redeem. Fee recipient: 0x6cba4751742f6989fa224b2dc5d5d52fcef98a34.
The hook uses no outside pool, token, price feed or service; every price it needs comes from its own pool.
Use mulDiv for every percentage calculation, including fees, shares, limits and price moves, to avoid intermediate multiplication overflow.
Keep the function names exactly as written so the storefront can show them. Composed with The Hooks Store block builder.

The hook does exactly the following, and nothing else:

Take 1.0% of the ETH side of every buy and sell as a hook fee, settled in ETH inside the swap that paid it (mint a claim when the PoolManager cannot pay it directly), and send it to 0x6cba4751742f6989fa224b2dc5d5d52fcef98a34. Expose claimFees(PoolId poolId) that anyone may call to redeem that pool's claims using the same distribution. 2. Replace only the Swap fee block's rate schedule, for the same buy and sell swaps: the rate starts at 10.0% at the pool's first swap and decreases linearly over 30 minutes of block timestamp to the Swap fee's 1.0%, then stays there. Expose currentFeeBps(PoolId poolId) as a view. In this hook, the token is the pool's non-ETH currency and its total supply is that token's totalSupply().
Every pool-dependent view, state, window and limit is keyed by PoolId and isolated per pool; pass the pool id to each pool-dependent function.
The hook does exactly the following, and nothing else:
1. If the absolute pool price move over the last 30 seconds of block timestamp exceeds 20%, reject every swap for the next 5 minutes of block timestamp, then resume automatically. Liquidity can still be removed during the pause. Track price history and the pause separately by PoolId. Expose haltedUntil(PoolId poolId) as a view.
Owner 0x6cba4751742f6989fa224b2dc5d5d52fcef98a34 is $owner. No owner functions, no backend signer, no upgrade path.
Hook fee rate: 0%.
The hook uses no outside pool, token, price feed or service; every price it needs comes from its own pool.
Use mulDiv for every percentage calculation, including fees, shares, limits and price moves, to avoid intermediate multiplication overflow.
Keep the function names exactly as written so the storefront can show them. Composed with The Hooks Store block builder.

Launch Pondside (POND) with a Uniswap v4 hook on Ethereum, paired with IMD.
Token: Pondside (POND), the standard launch token: 1,000,000,000 supply, 18 decimals, plain transfers, no owner functions.
beforeInitialize accepts only the IMD launch factory, passed as the constructor argument $factory; any other initialization reverts; the hook serves only the pool the factory initializes. Constructor arguments: the Ethereum PoolManager 0x000000000004444c5dc75cB358380D2e3dE08A90, $owner and $factory.
In this hook, the token is Pondside (POND), the launch token; its total supply is that token's totalSupply().
Every pool-dependent view, state, window and limit is keyed by PoolId and isolated per pool; pass the pool id to each pool-dependent function.
The hook does exactly the following, and nothing else:
1. Collect 1.0% of the IMD side of every swap into a jar held by the hook, tracked separately by PoolId and settled in IMD inside the swap that paid it (mint a claim when the PoolManager cannot pay it directly). When the jar holds at least 0.1 IMD, anyone may call buyback(PoolId poolId). Buy only inside buyback(), never inside a swap, from this same pool, with a price limit 3% above the pool price at the start of the call; keep any unspent IMD in that pool's jar and anyone may call it again. keep the bought tokens in the hook forever; no function can move them. Expose jar(PoolId poolId) as a view. Fees are computed on the amount actually traded; when the swap specifies its IMD amount and the pool fills only part of it, the swap reverts rather than overpaying.
Owner 0x6cba4751742f6989fa224b2dc5d5d52fcef98a34 is $owner. No owner functions, no backend signer, no upgrade path.
Fees are always taken from the IMD (pair currency) side, never from POND; a fee the PoolManager cannot pay directly is minted as a claim the recipient can redeem. Fee recipient: 0x6cba4751742f6989fa224b2dc5d5d52fcef98a34.
Keep every hook fee in IMD: do not convert the fee to ETH and do not use any other pool.
The launch token may be currency0 or currency1; handle both orders.
The hook uses no outside pool, token, price feed or service; every price it needs comes from its own pool.
Use mulDiv for every percentage calculation, including fees, shares, limits and price moves, to avoid intermediate multiplication overflow.
The launch factory ($factory) may always add liquidity and collect fees with a zero-change modify. Enable beforeInitialize and only the callbacks the behavior above needs.
Pool: 50% of the total supply seeds the pool; 10% goes to the swarm; the remaining 40% goes to 0x6cba4751742f6989fa224b2dc5d5d52fcef98a34. economics.poolBps=5000, in basis points of the total supply.
Keep the function names exactly as written so the storefront can show them. Composed with The Hooks Store block builder.

Launch Pondside (POND) with a Uniswap v4 hook on Ethereum, paired with IMD.
Token: Pondside (POND), the standard launch token: 1,000,000,000 supply, 18 decimals, plain transfers, no owner functions.
beforeInitialize accepts only the IMD launch factory, passed as the constructor argument $factory; any other initialization reverts; the hook serves only the pool the factory initializes. Constructor arguments: the Ethereum PoolManager 0x000000000004444c5dc75cB358380D2e3dE08A90, $owner and $factory.
In this hook, the token is Pondside (POND), the launch token; its total supply is that token's totalSupply().
Every pool-dependent view, state, window and limit is keyed by PoolId and isolated per pool; pass the pool id to each pool-dependent function.
The hook does exactly the following, and nothing else:
1. Take 1.0% of the IMD side of every buy and sell as a hook fee, settled in IMD inside the swap that paid it (mint a claim when the PoolManager cannot pay it directly), and send it to 0x6cba4751742f6989fa224b2dc5d5d52fcef98a34. Expose claimFees(PoolId poolId) that anyone may call to redeem that pool's claims using the same distribution. Fees are computed on the amount actually traded; when the swap specifies its IMD amount and the pool fills only part of it, the swap reverts rather than overpaying.
2. Replace the Swap fee's distribution: donate 50% of the Swap fee and Whale fee only, settled in IMD, back to that PoolId's in-range liquidity providers through the PoolManager's donate, and send the rest to the fee recipient (or split it if Split the fee is selected). If no liquidity is in range, the whole fee goes to the recipient under the same destination, including Split the fee when selected. Apply LP sharing first, then Split the fee; never share the Buyback jar or Prize pot.
Owner 0x6cba4751742f6989fa224b2dc5d5d52fcef98a34 is $owner. No owner functions, no backend signer, no upgrade path.
Fees are always taken from the IMD (pair currency) side, never from POND; a fee the PoolManager cannot pay directly is minted as a claim the recipient can redeem. Fee recipient: 0x6cba4751742f6989fa224b2dc5d5d52fcef98a34.
Keep every hook fee in IMD: do not convert the fee to ETH and do not use any other pool.
The launch token may be currency0 or currency1; handle both orders.
The hook uses no outside pool, token, price feed or service; every price it needs comes from its own pool.
Use mulDiv for every percentage calculation, including fees, shares, limits and price moves, to avoid intermediate multiplication overflow.
The launch factory ($factory) may always add liquidity and collect fees with a zero-change modify. Enable beforeInitialize and only the callbacks the behavior above needs.
Pool: 50% of the total supply seeds the pool; 10% goes to the swarm; the remaining 40% goes to 0x6cba4751742f6989fa224b2dc5d5d52fcef98a34. economics.poolBps=5000, in basis points of the total supply.
Keep the function names exactly as written so the storefront can show them. Composed with The Hooks Store block builder.

Use mulDiv for every percentage calculation, including fees, shares, limits and price moves, to avoid intermediate multiplication overflow.

Launch Pondside (POND) with a Uniswap v4 hook on Ethereum, paired with IMD.

Constructor arguments: the Ethereum PoolManager 0x000000000004444c5dc75cB358380D2e3dE08A90, $owner and $factory.
In this hook, the token is Pondside (POND), the launch token; its total supply is that token's totalSupply().
Every pool-dependent view, state, window and limit is keyed by PoolId and isolated per pool; pass the pool id to each pool-dependent function.
The hook does exactly the following, and nothing else:
1. Collect 2.0% of the IMD side of every buy into that PoolId's prize pot, settled in IMD inside the swap that paid it (mint a claim when the PoolManager cannot pay it directly). Periods last 1 hour(s) of block timestamp, starting at the pool's first swap. Anyone may call draw(PoolId poolId) to settle the most recent complete period: credit the whole pot to one recorded buyer, weighted by the total IMD each buyer spent. A period with no buyers rolls its pot into the next period. Use recorded cumulative weighted totals with a bounded winner lookup, never loop over every buyer. Expose pot(PoolId poolId) and nextDrawAt(PoolId poolId) as views. A wallet means tx.origin; several wallets or a shared relayer can defeat the limit. Fees are computed on the amount actually traded; when the swap specifies its IMD amount and the pool fills only part of it, the swap reverts rather than overpaying.
Owner 0x6cba4751742f6989fa224b2dc5d5d52fcef98a34 is $owner. No owner functions, no backend signer, no upgrade path.
Fees are always taken from the IMD (pair currency) side, never from POND; a fee the PoolManager cannot pay directly is minted as a claim the recipient can redeem. Fee recipient: 0x6cba4751742f6989fa224b2dc5d5d52fcef98a34.

Pool: 50% of the total supply seeds the pool; 10% goes to the swarm; the remaining 40% goes to 0x6cba4751742f6989fa224b2dc5d5d52fcef98a34. economics.poolBps=5000, in basis points of the total supply.
